name: Mk.gee
label: R&R
lede: A Jersey kid with a cassette four-track, a baritone Jaguar and a guitar-synth, who spent four years writing other people's hits before making the 33-minute album everyone argued about.

eras.title: Linwood kid, Portastudio kid
eras.text: A New Jersey teenager who records every instrument himself drops out of USC, posts a debut single and two EPs, and lands a major-label deal. Even then the sound is his own: cheap gear, cracked software, guitar played like a synth.

years.h: Out of Linwood, out of USC
years.p: Michael Gordon grew up in Linwood, New Jersey, graduated from Mainland Regional High School in 2015, then dropped out of USC's Thornton School of Music in 2016.
years.xp:
PhillyVoice has him starting piano and composition at age 5, with grandparents who ran a jazz society in nearby Somers Point. He told the paper that in Linwood it was never cool to make music, and that he formed a band with classmates years earlier.

Dazed has him growing up recording on cracked Ableton and still favoring what he calls cheap, bad gear, which forces him to solve problems. Sources disagree on his birth year: Wikipedia says 1996, Dazed says 1997.

years.h: First single: "I Know How You Get"
years.p: Gordon releases his debut single under the name Mk.gee, pronounced McGee.
Home-recorded songs including "Roll with the Punches" and "Over Here", and the EP that spells out how to say his name.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the EP on Orchard Ears with "Roll with the Punches", "Over Here" and "You" as singles. PhillyVoice says it got played on Frank Ocean's Blonded Radio, which is how a lot of people first heard of him.

years.h: Fool EP: a second one by Thanksgiving
years.p: Six months after the first EP comes a second on Orchard Ears, led by "Come On (You Know That I'm a Fool)" and "New Year".
play: Come On (You Know That I'm a Fool)

years.h: Interscope and IAMSOUND sign him, then send him on the road
years.p: Gordon signs with both IAMSOUND and Interscope, opens for Omar Apollo and Wallows, and plays his first festival, Pitchfork Paris.
years.xp: Wikipedia puts him on Apollo's Voyager Tour and Wallows' Nothing Happens Tour in 2019, with his festival debut at Pitchfork Music Festival Paris that year. The single "Untitled" is the first release under the new deal.

eras.title: The guy behind the guy
eras.text: His own records go quiet while other people's get his fingerprints: Omar Apollo, Dijon, a Charlotte Day Wilson song that ends up sampled by Drake and Travis Scott. The partnership with Dijon starts here.

years.h: A Museum of Contradiction: a 25-minute mixtape that sounds like a dare
years.p: His major-label debut is a mixtape of bedroom funk and psychedelia, preceded in February by the single "cz". NME gave it four stars.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists it at 24 minutes 45 seconds, on IAMSOUND and Interscope, with Andrew Sarlo engineering and mixing and Joseph Thornalley co-producing ">;0" with Vegyn. NME's Rhys Buchanan called it a release that "merges genres from different worlds with both maturity and ease".

years.h: Co-producing [[Dijon|cceea21d-f3ec-4586-be7a-d2e939c15c78]]'s Absolutely, and a sample heard round the rap world
years.p: Gordon co-produces Dijon Duenas' debut album, and co-writes "Mountains" with Charlotte Day Wilson, later sampled on Drake and Travis Scott's "Fair Trade".
years.xp:
Wikipedia calls Absolutely (November 2021) self-produced by Dijon "alongside frequent collaborator Mk.gee". The Dijon and Mk.gee partnership is the spine of everything that follows, including Two Star.

Wikipedia also credits Gordon with co-producing Omar Apollo's 2020 mixtape Apolonio.

eras.title: Two Star, one Portastudio
eras.text: After four years of silence under his own name, Gordon releases a debut album that critics cannot stop describing and cannot quite place. It makes him the year's most argued-over guitarist.

years.p: The first preview of the album drops as two songs at once, funk-leaning and lo-fi. Rolling Stone's Joshua Minsoo Kim later calls "How Many Miles" the album's highlight.

years.src: Wikipedia: Two Star & the Dream Police
years.h: Second double single: "Are You Looking Up" and "You Got It"
years.p: Dazed ranks "Are You Looking Up" No. 12 of 2023 and The Fader puts "You Got It" at No. 26, before the album even exists.
years.xp: Wikipedia notes "You Got It" later shows up in the third season of The Bear. A five-date "Inside Each of Us Are Two Stars" tour had opened at Music Hall of Williamsburg in Brooklyn on October 16.

years.cap: Cover of Two Star & the Dream Police
years.src: Album of the Year · Wikipedia: Two Star & the Dream Police · Dazed · Rolling Stone
years.h: Two Star & the Dream Police: 12 songs, 33 minutes, nobody sounds like it
years.p: Pitchfork gave the debut album a 7.8 and ranked it No. 18 of 2024. Gordon mixed it himself and co-produced with [[Dijon|cceea21d-f3ec-4586-be7a-d2e939c15c78]] on R&R.
years.xp:
The Pitchfork score is 78 on Album of the Year's critic list (review by Brady Brickner-Wood), who called it a "magnificent debut album". Metacritic shows 83 from four reviews. Anthony Fantano's Needle Drop gave it 60, the low score in that list, while the Guardian and the Arts Desk gave 100.

Dazed says Andrew Sarlo helped with arranging and Gordon played everything else. Rolling Stone points to how he uses silence: on "New Low" he "doesn't utter a word during the final 30 seconds".

Mastering is split between Heba Kadry ("How Many Miles", "Candy") and Simon Lancelot. Wikipedia lists the label as R&R.

years.src: Wikipedia: Two Star & the Dream Police · Year-End Lists
years.h: Everybody's list: No. 1 at Clash, Dazed and the New York Times
years.p: Clash, Dazed and Jon Caramanica of the New York Times put it first; the New Yorker and Gorilla vs. Bear had it No. 2. Pitchfork's own list had it 18th.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's reception section also lists it No. 3 at the Los Angeles Times, No. 7 at the Line of Best Fit, and top 20 at NME, the Guardian and Rolling Stone. In October 2024 Pitchfork put it No. 91 on its 100 Best Albums of the 2020s So Far, less than five years into the decade.

"Alesis" was the most-listed single, No. 1 of the year at Coup De Main and Vulture.

q: He has found things to do on the guitar that are like nobody else.
years.h: Eric Clapton, asked who excites him on guitar, picks Mk.gee
years.p: Clapton compares Gordon's arrival to Prince's. Gordon plays a Jaguar strung as a baritone, through a Roland guitar-synth pickup and a Portastudio 424 used as a preamp.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, Clapton called Gordon unique and said he can "do it live" too. Gordon's rig, also per Wikipedia: Fender Jaguar strung as a baritone with flatwounds, a Roland GK-2A divided pickup into a VG-8, and the Portastudio's cassette-style clipping left on purpose.

years.src: Wikipedia: Two Star & the Dream Police
yt: Alesis, live at the Fonda, Los Angeles
years.p: Vancouver to Melbourne, after 18 North American dates in April and May. Live clips like "Alesis" at the Fonda in Los Angeles become their own event.
years.xp:
Billboard wrote that his Los Angeles show proved "good music alone can carry a great show". The Guardian described a room of newfound obsessives with arena rock energy, and NME called London an almost religious experience.

Wikipedia tracks these from the tour dates and the review round-ups cited in the album article.

years.cap: Mk.gee at House of Blues Dallas, September 2024 · Wikimedia
years.h: Saturday Night Live: "Alesis" and a song nobody has heard
years.p: He plays "Alesis" and the new standalone single "Rockman", released October 18, and "Rockman" becomes his first charting single.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says Gordon co-wrote "Rockman" with Zack Sekoff, who plays in his live band, and produced it himself. It peaked at No. 24 on Adult Alternative Airplay, No. 25 on Alternative Airplay and No. 30 on Rock & Alternative Airplay. It was nominated for Record of the Year at the 2025 Libera Awards.

His first TV performance had been Jimmy Kimmel Live! on April 11, with "Are You Looking Up".

eras.title: The guitar on everyone's record
eras.text: The aesthetic that Two Star made unmistakable spreads into pop's biggest rooms, with Gordon credited on records by Justin Bieber and Bon Iver while he keeps playing festivals under his own name.

q: Anything that comes out of his mouth is pop music.
years.h: Justin Bieber's "Daisies" lands at No. 2, with Mk.gee in the credits
years.p: Gordon co-produces and co-writes the lead single from Swag with Dijon, among others; it peaks at No. 2 on the Hot 100 and is Grammy-nominated.
years.xp:
Wikipedia credits Dijon, Mk.gee, Eddie Benjamin, Carter Lang, Dylan Wiggins and Daniel Chetrit as producers, with Tobias Jesso Jr. as a songwriter. Tonitruale reports Mk.gee receives official credit on "Daisies" while his guitar sound runs through the album. Gordon also co-wrote "Love Song" on Swag II.

Asked about writing for pop stars, Gordon said anything that comes out of Bieber's mouth is pop music, and "you can really do pretty wild stuff behind that".

years.h: A co-write on Bon Iver's "From", and festivals across two continents
years.p: Gordon co-writes "From" on Bon Iver's Sable, Fable with Justin Vernon and Tobias Jesso Jr.; he plays Governors Ball, Lollapalooza, Øya and Austin City Limits.
years.xp: Wikipedia also lists him on the BBC's Sound of 2025 nominees and Libera Awards nominations for Best Breakthrough Artist and Record of the Year. Dijon, his main partner, released his second album Baby on August 15, 2025, and appears on Bon Iver's "Day One".
